candidates.title: Checking only the localization at the prime ideal \(P=(x,y)A[t]\) is insufficien
candidates.quote: さらに $A[t]$ もゴレンシュタイン環であることを、\ref{ring:polynomial-invariance} を使わずに素イデアル $P=(x,y)A[t]$ での局所化について確かめよ。
candidates.problem: Checking only the localization at the prime ideal \(P=(x,y)A[t]\) is insufficient to prove that the non-local ring \(A[t]\) is Gorenstein. For a non-local Noetherian ring, one must show that all localizations at prime ideals (equivalently, at all maximal ideals) are Gorenstein. The ideal \(P\) is not maximal—\(A[t]/P \cong k[t]\)—and there are maximal ideals such as \((x,y,t)\) (or more generally \((x,y,f(t))\) for irreducible \(f(t)\)) whose localizations must also be checked. The localization at \(P\) is \(0\)-dimensional, while the maximal localizations are \(1\)-dimensional, so verifying only \(P\) does not address the maximal ideals.
candidates.proposed_fix: To correctly verify that \(A[t]\) is Gorenstein without using polynomial invariance, check localizations at all maximal ideals, e.g. at \(M=(x,y,f(t))\) for each irreducible \(f(t)\). For such an \(M\), \(f(t)\) is a non-zero-divisor and the quotient \(A[t]/(f(t))\) is a \(0\)-dimensional Gorenstein ring (its socle is generated by \(xy\)); hence \(A[t]_{M}\) is Gorenstein. Also check the minimal prime \(P=(x,y)A[t]\) (or note it follows similarly). Checking only \(P\) is not enough.

second_opinion.reason: Checking only the localization \(A[t]_{P}\) does not establish that the nonlocal ring \(A[t]\) is Gorenstein; one must check localizations at all prime ideals, equivalently at all maximal ideals. Since \(P=(x,y)A[t]\) is not maximal, maximal ideals such as \((x,y,t)\) also require verification. Thus the claimed omission is a real mathematical issue.
